    Building on Nemotron 3.5 Parse: Open Data, Fine-Tuning, and Faster Inference

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1302 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Hugging Face

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We recently released NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Parse, a compact document model that turns page images into structured data for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agents.
    • Industry observers note that now we’re building on that release with synthetic training datasets, a fine-tuning recipe, and a DFlash2 speculator for faster inference.
    • In a recent development, parse extracts content from pages of documents into reading order, assigns content classes such as headings, paragraphs, tables, and charts, and returns bounding boxes that locate the content.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We recently released NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Parse, a compact document model that turns page images into structured data for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agents.

    Industry observers note that now we’re building on that release with synthetic training datasets, a fine-tuning recipe, and a DFlash2 speculator for faster inference. We’re also sharing how we trained Parse 3.5: first teaching document understanding through supervised fine-tuning, then using reinforcement learning to improve accuracy, consistency, and reliable completion.

    In a recent development, parse extracts content from pages of documents into reading order, assigns content classes such as headings, paragraphs, tables, and charts, and returns bounding boxes that locate the content. Tables and charts become structured records that can power downstream document processing applications.

    Industry observers note that figure 1. Actual model output from a synthetic operations brief, showing the connection between the page and its structured representation.

    Sources indicate that this latest version of Parse significantly extends its ability to read charts and tables, especially in more difficult and ambiguous cases. For example, bar charts or other plots that do not have any marked numeric values. The model is able to infer values by looking at the axes and height of the bar to derive these. Tables can be especially tricky because the structure is so meaningful, a shifted row or column can totally change the interpretation and meaning. These advancements have been largely powered by synthetic data generation, rendering variations of charts and tables with known ground truth and then training our model to reverse this process.

    We are open-sourcing three datasets used in the Parse 3.5 training:.

    Synthetic Charts V1 — 9.98M examples: rendered charts and structured annotations for learning categories, series, and numerical values.

    Synthetic Tables V1 — 1M examples: rendered HTML tables with targets that preserve rows, columns, headers, and cell relationships.

    OCR Synthetic Multilingual v2 — 7.9M examples: synthetic document pages with Parse-format targets across varied fonts and layouts, for multilingual OCR and structured page reading.

    It has been revealed that each release includes images, annotations, generation documentation, and the training format. Use these pairs to fine-tune document models or create new variations for a target document type or language.

    Sources indicate that figure 2. Parse recovers 18, 27, 39, and 54 from the chart geometry.

    According to recent reports, we trained Parse 3.5 with two phases of training. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) spanning text, layout, tables, charts, and multilingual documents. Learning to predict structured targets established the general capability of reading a page and representing its contents.

    It has been revealed that we then continued with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Rewards check the quality of sampled extractions. For example, a chart extraction can earn a better reward for recovering the correct series and values, producing a usable structure, and finishing without repeatedly generating the same content.

    Recent findings suggest that A difficult page can have several valid representations. These checks give the model flexibility to find a correct answer without prescribing one exact token sequence, while discouraging looping and unfinished output.

    Figure 3. A controlled comparison of SFT and GRPO with matched evaluation settings. These are development checkpoints, separate from the final released model. Loop counts use a repetition check. Methods.

    In a recent development, the matched comparison indicates the benefit: loop-flagged outputs fall from 126 to 29 pages—about 77% fewer—and outputs reaching the 9,000-token limit fall from 185 to 35. Overall score improves from 66.24 to 71.38, including +5.18 points in tables and +4.15 in charts.

    Sources indicate that A parser must generate substantial text and structure for every page. Alongside the training work, we optimized how Parse 3.5 processes images and decodes those outputs.

    Recent findings suggest that naViT preprocessing adapts the input shape to the page. A visual adapter compresses the image sequence, and the text decoder consumes it as a prefix, replacing encoder–decoder cross-attention. Grouped-query attention with eight key/value heads (GQA-8) reduces the decoder’s attention-cache memory.

    The built-in multi-token prediction (MTP) head supplies one-token lookahead. Our DFlash2 speculator goes further: a small draft model proposes up to 32 tokens ahead, and Parse verifies the proposals together. In the measured 32-token configuration, it averages about 14 accepted draft tokens, or roughly 15 output tokens of progress per verification step including the target token.

    Figure 4. Native single-pass throughput on one H200, BF16, using the same 2,078 pages. Parse 2.0 uses one trial per point; Parse 3.5 indicates three-trial medians. Arrows show the gain from Parse 3.5 base to DFlash2. Measurement details.

    Sources indicate that in the native single-pass benchmark on one H200 in BF16, DFlash2 increased throughput 7.62× at concurrency 1 and 1.52× at concurrency 512, compared with Parse 3.5 with speculative decoding disabled. At 512, Parse 3.5 reaches 13.48 pages/s without speculation and 20.44 pages/s with DFlash2, versus 2.98 for Parse 2.0. Those are 4.53× and 6.86× the Parse 2.0 throughput, respectively.

    Sources indicate that fast parsing gives us room to revisit difficult regions. Start with a full-page prediction, then add focused reprocessing where the document needs it:.

    Single pass - Parse the full page once for text, layout, tables, and charts.

    In a recent development, double pass - use for dense tables and small chart details. Crop the table and chart regions found by the parser, re-parse them at higher detail, and merge the refinements into the page output.

    Triple pass - Instead of only using the models full page parsing bounding boxes, use a second pass of the model in detection mode in order to get verification that all boxes have been accurately found and text has not been missed and re-extract any found charts or tables in a third pass.

    Industry observers note that figure 5. Additional stages focus computation on difficult regions. Multiple crops can require multiple requests.

    Sources indicate that in the published reference evaluation, double and triple pass add 2.18 and 2.46 ParseBench points over single pass. The additional work lets applications trade some throughput for better extraction in difficult regions. Reference results and serving measurements.

    We are sharing a Parse fine-tuning recipe that takes developers through paired data generation, NeMo Automodel SFT, and NeMo RL GRPO, using vLLM to generate candidate answers.

    The worked example uses a synthetic dental form with an odontogram: a chart showing teeth, planned procedures, and affected tooth surfaces. Before adaptation, Parse reads the printed tooth numbers but misses the intended procedure table. SFT teaches it to associate each marked tooth with a procedure and its placement on the tooth.

    Figure 6. A recorded recipe example: after SFT, all six chart rows match the target. Full image and native training label.

    RLVR then reinforces accuracy and consistent completion. In the dental reference run, the estimated first-attempt success rate (sampled pass@1) rose from 0.00% for the base model to 95.85% after SFT and 96.58% after RLVR.

    Figure 7. Matched evaluation on 256 held-out forms from the same synthetic generator, with eight samples per page. Success requires natural completion, exact chart content, and error-free normalized page text. Evaluation protocol.

    In a recent development, to adapt the recipe, supply your own image/label pairs and a verifier: checks that determine whether an extraction is correct. The included document reward components cover text fidelity, bounding boxes, tables, chart facts, and completion. Combine the components relevant to your task, add schema checks, and use completion and repetition checks to discourage looping or unfinished output.

    We are excited that the community has extended and improved Parse for Thai, Persian/Farsi, and Arabic already and we hope that these additional datasets and fine-tuning recipes will help encourage these efforts and future models.

    We thank Denis Ovchinnikov for his work on vLLM integration and independent performance validation, Oliver Holworthy for improving the fine-tuning recipe's runtime setup and reproducibility, and Bo Liu for technical review.

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (880 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dev ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: AWS Security Alerts in an Afternoon: 5 Audit Commands and One CloudFormation Template

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (880 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • On November 28, 2025, Sysdig watched an attacker take test credentials from a public S3 bucket and have their own code running in the victim's Lambda function eight minutes later.
    • That is fast, but it is not unusual.
    • Industry observers note that most of us have no security team.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    On November 28, 2025, Sysdig watched an attacker take test credentials from a public S3 bucket and have their own code running in the victim's Lambda function eight minutes later. Admin access followed in under ten.

    That is fast, but it is not unusual. Unit 42 leaked keys to public GitHub on purpose and saw them used within five minutes. Clutch Security measured 6.6 minutes on average.

    Industry observers note that most of us have no security team. This post is the setup I would do in an afternoon instead:.

    Sources indicate that prices are for US East (N. Virginia), read on November 26, 2026.

    CloudTrail delivers within about 5 minutes of an API call on average, and AWS says that time is not guaranteed. So this pipeline tells you at roughly minute five. Keep that number in mind for the last section.

    All five commands are read-only.

    CloudTrail's free 90-day event history already holds a lot. This is one account's console sign-ins, with the names changed. Two rows are the root user, and nothing on this page tells anyone.

    Two results look like failures and are really findings:.

    Industry observers note that create the trail in the console. The docs say all trails created there are multi-Region, and the console sets up the bucket policy for you.

    GuardDuty has to be enabled per Region. The Regions you never deploy to are the ones an attacker will use, so enable all of them:.

    It has been revealed that that loop changes your account, and the 30-day trial starts per Region when you run it. Check the Usage page in the GuardDuty console before the trial ends.

    Save this as aws-security-alerts.yaml.

    Deploy it in us-east-1 first (see trap 1 below), then confirm the subscription email SNS sends you:.

    Industry observers note that what I verified, and what I did not. The template passes aws cloudformation validate-template, and both event patterns matched the right sample events in the test below. I have not deployed this exact stack to a live account, so I have not watched an email arrive from it. Deploy it to a sandbox account first.

    AttachUserPolicy earns its place twice. It also fires when AWS quarantines a leaked key, because the quarantine is a policy attached to the user. The policy ARN is in the event's requestParameters.

    Recent findings suggest that some of these are noisy on a busy account. AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress fires for every rule, not just 0.0.0.0/0. Start with everything, then trim what your own pipeline does every day.

    aws events test-event-pattern checks a pattern against a sample event without creating anything. This is how I tested the sign-in rule:.

    According to recent reports, I ran nine cases across the two rules. Root sign-in, IAM user without MFA, StopLogging and CreateAccessKey matched. An IAM user with MFA, a failed login, a single sign-on session and DescribeInstances did not.

    According to recent reports, 1. IAM lives in us-east-1. IAM, STS and CloudFront are global services, and CloudTrail records their events in US East (N. Virginia). A rule in eu-west-1 will never see CreateAccessKey. Root sign-ins land in us-east-1, us-east-2 or us-west-2. Deploy the stack in us-east-1, then in those two, then in every Region you run workloads in.

    In a recent development, 2. MFAUsed is always No for single sign-on. AWS only sets it for IAM people and root. Without the IAMUser filter, every SSO login emails you.

    It has been revealed that 3. S3 event names differ from the API. The API call DeletePublicAccessBlock appears in CloudTrail as DeleteBucketPublicAccessBlock or DeleteAccountPublicAccessBlock. Match the CloudTrail name.

    Sources indicate that 4. Read-only calls need a different rule state. A rule in the default ENABLED state does not match read-only management events. To alert on something like GetSecretValue, set the rule's state to ENABLED_WITH_ALL_CLOUDTRAIL_MANAGEMENT_EVENTS. You also need a trail that is logging, or none of these rules receive anything.

    Recent findings suggest that one more: the docs spell the sign-in detail-type two ways (AWS Console Sign In via CloudTrail and AWS Console Signin via CloudTrail). The pattern above matches on source: aws.signin so it does not depend on either.

    AWS shipped two things that cover some of this:.

    Sources indicate that you now get an email at about minute five. It is a block of JSON. It does not say whether that CreateAccessKey was your deploy pipeline or a stranger, and at 3 a.m. nobody reads it until morning.

    In a recent development, that gap is the real work. Someone has to look at who did it, from where, and what else they did in the same few minutes. Staffing that around the clock takes 4.2 people per seat (168 hours in a week, 40 in a working one), which is about $542,556 a year at the US median analyst wage.

    Disclosure: I work on Jutsu, which does that first investigation in software and asks before it acts. The longer version of this post, with the cost comparison and screenshots, is on the Jutsu blog.

    Whatever you choose, decide who answers the alert. A rule nobody reads is a log.

    What would you add to the event list? I left out RunInstances and PutRolePolicy to keep the noise down, and I am not sure that was right.

    • In a recent development, if the README links to a deployment guide, you can follow the link, read the diagram at full width, and hit Back.

    My code is on the left, my AI chat is on the right, and somehow I’m trying to read a Mermaid diagram in a third VS Code pane. By the time I’ve dragged the divider far enough to read the labels, I can barely see my code.

    Sources indicate that that’s why I built Browsedown. Right-click your docs/ folder in VS Code and choose Open in Browser. It serves the Markdown locally and opens your README in a browser tab, with the subfolders in a sidebar. There’s nothing to configure or push first.

    In a recent development, if the README links to a deployment guide, you can follow the link, read the diagram at full width, and hit Back. On a team call, that’s the tab I’d share when someone asks, “What happens after we merge?”.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Almost four in five people with chronic migraine have low levels of this vitamin.
    • Almost four in five people with chronic migraine have low levels of this vitamin.
    • Frequent headaches are linked to lower vitamin D levels.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Almost four in five people with chronic migraine have low levels of this vitamin.

    Almost four in five people with chronic migraine have low levels of this vitamin.

    Frequent headaches are linked to lower vitamin D levels.

    People with chronic migraine have lower levels than those with occasional migraines or no headache disorder.

    Lower vitamin D is also associated with greater muscle tenderness.

    The vitamin helps muscles and nerves function, making it relevant to understanding pain.

    One possibility is that low levels amplify sensitivity to pain, although this remains an explanation to investigate.

    The research compared around 150 adults, divided equally between chronic migraine, episodic migraine and a group without headache disorders.

    Blood tests showed low vitamin D in 78 percent of the chronic migraine group, compared with 60 percent of those with episodic migraine and 46 percent of the comparison group.

    Average levels were lowest in chronic migraine and highest among those without headaches.

    Chronic migraine means headaches on at least 15 days a month for more than three months, with migraine features on at least eight days.

    These headaches can change in character, even within the same day, and can include pain resembling tension headaches.

    Lower vitamin D levels were associated with more tenderness when muscles were pressed.

    The researchers suggest that muscular discomfort and changes in pain processing could interact, potentially helping sustain headaches.

    However, the association could also run in the opposite direction: people with migraine may spend less time outdoors because of light sensitivity or fatigue.

    The findings do not establish that supplements prevent migraines.

    Vitamin D’s established functions extend beyond maintaining strong bones.

    It helps the body absorb calcium, supports muscle movement and allows nerves to carry messages between the brain and the body.

    Deficiency can cause a condition called osteomalacia in adults, involving bone pain and muscle weakness.

    The body produces vitamin D when sunlight reaches the skin, while food provides another source.

    Oily fish, including salmon and mackerel, are among the best natural sources, while egg yolks contain smaller amounts.

    Some breakfast cereals and other foods are fortified with the vitamin.

    People who rarely expose their skin to sunlight can have more difficulty obtaining enough.

    A blood test measures vitamin D status, helping distinguish a nutritional shortage from symptoms with other possible explanations.

    The study was published in the journal Cephalalgia Reports (Prakash et al., 2026).

    It has been revealed that psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean.

    #206812. Giving a coding agent test results it can act on: JUnit XML, go test -json and a short failure summary

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (684 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dev ↗ Open Full Page

    Giving a coding agent test results it can act on: JUnit XML, go test -json and a short failure summary

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (684 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that most coding agents spend a large share of their turns in one loop: change code, run the tests, read the result, change code again.
    • Recent findings suggest that test runners already know the answer in structured form.
    • Three common runners, each writing a report next to its normal output:.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that most coding agents spend a large share of their turns in one loop: change code, run the tests, read the result, change code again. The quality of that loop depends on what "read the result" means. An exit code of 1 tells the model something failed and nothing about what. The full log tells it everything, at a cost in tokens and attention, and the one assertion that matters is somewhere in the middle.

    Recent findings suggest that test runners already know the answer in structured form. Most can write a report that lists every test, its status, and for each failure a message and a stack trace. This post reveals how to get those reports out of a sandbox and turn them into a tool result built for a model: the counts, the first few failures, and a clear signal when the run did not finish at all.

    Three common runners, each writing a report next to its normal output:.

    Jest can write the same JUnit XML through the separately installed jest-junit reporter. JUnit XML is the closest thing the ecosystem has to a shared format: a testsuite holds testcase elements, and a failing case has a failure or error child with a message attribute and the trace as text. Skipped cases have a skipped child.

    In a recent development, go's format is a stream instead. Each line is an event with an Action such as run, output, pass, fail or skip, plus the Package and Test it belongs to. A test's output arrives as a series of output events before its fail.

    In a recent development, the parser below reads either format and returns the same shape: totals, the first five failures, and how many more were left out. Each failure's message and details are cut to a fixed size. It uses the fast-xml-parser package for XML.

    A few choices here are deliberate:.

    The tool that runs the tests should distinguish three outcomes, because the right next step is different for each:.

    In a recent development, here is that tool for pytest with the Sandscale TypeScript SDK. run returns exitCode, stdout, stderr, timedOut and oomKilled, and readFile reads the report back:.

    It has been revealed that the stale report is deleted before each run. Without that, a run that crashes before pytest writes anything would read the previous run's report and tell the model its tests failed for old reasons, or passed.

    Recent findings suggest that combine the exit code with the report rather than trusting either alone. A runner can exit non-zero with no failing tests listed, for example pytest exits with a distinct code when it collected no tests at all, and the summary's total of zero is the clue the model needs.

    According to recent reports, once the model knows which test failed, it rarely needs the whole suite again. Say so in the tool description, and give it a way to rerun a subset:.

    Narrow reruns are cheaper and give shorter, clearer reports. Run the full suite again before the agent declares the task done.

    Recent findings suggest that everything in this post runs inside the sandbox, under the agent's control. That is the right place for the edit-test loop, and the wrong place to decide whether a change is safe to merge. An agent can edit a test until it passes, mark it skipped, or change the configuration that decides which tests run. None of that is malicious; it is what optimizing for "tests pass" looks like.

    Recent findings suggest that A Sandscale sandbox gives each run its own Firecracker microVM, so test suites the agent wrote or changed run against their own kernel and filesystem, with the network mode defaulting to none. The builtin:base template has Python 3, Node.js, Git and a C compiler; your project's own test dependencies go in with the project. The result fields this post relies on, exitCode, timedOut and oomKilled, come straight from run, and the command and the files read back are recorded in the audit log.

    Originally published on the Sandscale blog.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the llama.cpp × AMD Benchmark dashboard is available on Hugging Face. It lets you track prompt processing and text generation performance across llama.cpp builds, models, and quantizations, so you can explore how local inference performs on AMD Ryzen and Radeon hardware.

    Recent findings suggest that local inference performance changes as models, kernels, and builds evolve. We want those changes to be easy to inspect for any AMD developer: pick a hardware, a model and a build, compare quantizations, and follow performance over time. The benchmark workflow and underlying results are public, so you can also inspect how we benchmark inference performance.

    You can choose Hardware, Model, and llama.cpp build in the Configuration sidebar. The current hardware choices are Radeon 8060S (gfx1151) and Radeon AI Pro R9700S (gfx1201).

    The dashboard shows two separate tests, both measured in tokens per second:.

    According to recent reports, both tests start at context depth zero (n_depth=0). PP512 measures processing 512 input tokens without generation; TG128 measures generating 128 tokens without a pre-existing context. The plotted value is the mean throughput (avg_ts). These are useful reference workloads, while the Context scaling tab lets you explore token generation throughput as the context grows.

    It has been revealed that we benchmark the prebuilt binaries distributed through llama-install.sh, the build and installation project behind llama.app. The public gfx1151 and gfx1201 workflows are scheduled weekly and run the standard benchmarks using the llama-bench tool with Flash Attention on and off, with 10 repetitions per configuration.

    In a recent development, the model set evolves and at the moment includes Inkling 2 Mini, Qwen, Gemma, gpt-oss, and LFM models, covering both dense and mixture-of-experts architectures. Available GGUF formats include Q4_K_M, Q8_0, other quantizations, and higher-precision formats such as BF16 and F16.

    The explorer reads directly from the public ggml-org/install.sh-benches-data Storage Bucket on Hugging Face. The data source link beside the chart title opens the folder for the selected build, hardware, and model.

    Industry observers note that standard results use ///.jsonl. Workload sweeps use the same folder -tg.jsonl filename.

    Use them to investigate a result, make your own charts, or compare with a local run.

    Thanks to the AMD team for providing test infrastructure and helping validate the setup! Try the dashboard, inspect the data, and let us know which models and workloads you would like to see next.

    Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies.
    • An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers.
    • Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

    An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

    Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers. Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

    Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

    It has been revealed that performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

    In a recent development, smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile people by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a massive opportunity.

    The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

    An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

    In a recent development, publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

    A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program. Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

    Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

    Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:.

    Recent findings suggest that one of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

    Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:.

    According to recent reports, commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

    Who manages your affiliate program?

    Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

    Run Local Audio Stem Separation with Stem Separator and Docker

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1301 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If you want to remove vocals from a song, isolate drums, or export several instrument tracks, sending audio to a third-party API is not your only option.
    • It has been revealed that this tutorial uses the project's stable v1.0.0 release and Docker Compose.
    • Sources indicate that clone the repository, start the default Compose service, open http://localhost:7860, and upload an MP3, WAV, FLAC, M4A, AAC, OGG, or OPUS file.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you want to remove vocals from a song, isolate drums, or export several instrument tracks, sending audio to a third-party API is not your only option. Stem Separator is an open-source, self-hosted web application that runs the separation pipeline on your own machine, homelab, or NAS.

    It has been revealed that this tutorial uses the project's stable v1.0.0 release and Docker Compose. You will start the CPU version, verify its health endpoint, upload a supported audio file through the browser, and understand when the NVIDIA GPU configuration is appropriate.

    Sources indicate that clone the repository, start the default Compose service, open http://localhost:7860, and upload an MP3, WAV, FLAC, M4A, AAC, OGG, or OPUS file. The default mode separates vocals and music. Stem Separator stores model weights in a named Docker volume and writes job output to ./data/output.

    Recent findings suggest that the crucial boundary is that this is local processing, not an anonymous public service. The application does not include built-in authentication or rate limiting, so keep it on localhost or a trusted LAN unless you add an authenticated reverse proxy.

    Industry observers note that the CPU deployment includes FFmpeg in the image. You do not need to install Python, PyTorch, or FFmpeg on the host for this path.

    The repository is MIT licensed and the stable release used here is v1.0.0. The project README is the source for the commands and configuration discussed below: paladini/stem-separator.

    Clone the repository and build the service:.

    The service listens on port 7860. Open http://localhost:7860 in a browser.

    Industry observers note that the first build can take time because the image installs dependencies. The first separation can also take longer while the selected model downloads.

    Check the container and its health endpoint:.

    A healthy response reports the detected device, whether FFmpeg is available, and the active and queued job counts. If FFmpeg is unavailable, the endpoint reports a degraded state instead of pretending that a separation can succeed.

    Inspect the application logs while the first model is loading:.

    Stop following the logs with Ctrl+C. The container keeps running.

    In the web interface, select an audio file and choose a separation goal. The default Vocals & Music mode uses the curated MDX-Net Inst HQ 3 model and produces vocals and music tracks. The interface only exposes tracks that the selected model can produce, which avoids requesting outputs that the model cannot generate.

    Choose an output format supported by the application:.

    In a recent development, submit the job and wait for the stages shown in the interface: preparing audio, loading the model, separating tracks, and exporting files. When processing finishes, preview tracks in the browser or download individual files and the ZIP archive.

    Recent findings suggest that the default Compose file maps the host directory ./data/output to /data/output in the container. That directory holds job state and exported tracks, so the results remain available when the container restarts. Model weights use the named volume stem-separator-models, which prevents a model from being downloaded again after every container recreation.

    The default Compose configuration is intentionally conservative:.

    These settings cap upload size and duration, reject jobs when disk space is too low, limit concurrent processing to one job, and bound the waiting queue. Completed or failed job folders are retained for 24 hours by default.

    Recent findings suggest that the default model is a practical CPU starting point. The repository also documents a BS-Roformer model of about 610 MB, recommended for an NVIDIA GPU because CPU processing can be slow. Model file size is not the same as runtime memory, so treat the RAM and VRAM guidance as a baseline, not a guarantee.

    Industry observers note that the project provides a separate Compose override for NVIDIA CUDA. The host needs an updated NVIDIA driver and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit installation. Verify that Docker can see the GPU before starting Stem Separator:.

    Then start the GPU image with both Compose files:.

    Industry observers note that the override replaces the CPU image, requests all GPUs, and keeps the same port and mounts. Do not run both stacks in the same checkout because both publish port 7860.

    Sources indicate that the Docker configuration supports CPU and NVIDIA CUDA deployments. The README does not claim verified Docker acceleration for Apple Silicon MPS/CoreML, AMD ROCm, Intel graphics, or Windows DirectML. If you need those paths, evaluate the native Python setup separately instead of assuming the Docker image will pass through the host accelerator.

    It has been revealed that stem Separator places a small web application in front of python-audio-separator. Its catalog maps friendly goals such as Vocals & Music to a verified model and a set of output tracks. The job manager validates the input, creates an isolated job directory, runs the engine, and exposes status and download endpoints.

    That separation is useful operationally. A malformed filename or unsupported extension can be rejected before inference, and a low-disk condition can stop a job before it consumes more storage. Engine failures can return as actionable application errors rather than unfiltered stack traces.

    Check the logs and verify that the container has its bundled FFmpeg available. For a native Python installation, install FFmpeg and confirm that both ffmpeg and ffprobe are on PATH. A degraded health response is a signal to fix the media dependency before submitting a job.

    Sources indicate that the first use of a model downloads its weights. Watch docker compose logs -f, check available disk space, and remember that the model cache is mounted at /data/models. Deleting the named volume forces the downloads again.

    Start with the default Vocals & Music model, reduce concurrency if you changed it, or choose the Force CPU option exposed by the application. The larger studio model and multi-instrument modes need more memory. A GPU does not remove the need to size the host and its VRAM correctly.

    Run docker compose ps and inspect the port mapping. If another application owns port 7860, change the host side of the mapping in a local Compose override, then use the matching browser URL. Keep the container port at 7860 unless you also change the health check and application configuration consistently.

    The README documents local processing, filename sanitization, isolated UUID job directories, and path-containment checks for downloads. These safeguards are not a complete deployment security model.

    It has been revealed that there is no built-in authentication or per-IP rate limiting. Do not expose this service directly to the public internet. If remote access is necessary, put it behind a reverse proxy with HTTPS, authentication, request-size limits, and rate limits. Also review the licenses and usage rights for the audio files and model weights you process.

    According to recent reports, the project is designed to process audio locally. In the Docker workflow, input files, model inference, and exports stay in the host's container volumes unless you add another integration yourself.

    In a recent development, no. The CPU Compose file is the default. A compatible NVIDIA GPU can accelerate supported workloads, but it adds host driver and toolkit requirements.

    Run docker compose down. The named model volume and the ./data/output bind mount remain unless you explicitly remove them.

    Stem Separator turns local audio stem separation into a repeatable Docker workflow: one Compose command, a browser interface, persistent model storage, bounded jobs, and explicit CPU/GPU tradeoffs. Start with the CPU deployment, verify /health, and move to the NVIDIA override only when the host prerequisites and memory budget are clear.

    What would make a self-hosted separator more useful for your workflow: batch-folder processing, an authenticated multi-user mode, or a more detailed quality comparison between models?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry.
    • Recent findings suggest that personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time.
    • It has been revealed that seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry. It’s easier than you think to start leveraging artificial intelligence tools in your marketing strategy. Here are 11 AI marketing tools every marketer should start using today.

    Recent findings suggest that personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time. The platform uses an algorithm to identify each contact’s top three interests, which are updated in real-time based on recent site activity.

    It has been revealed that seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes. Choosing the best day and time to send an email is always a gamble. And while some days of the week generally get higher open rates than others, you’ll never be able to nail down a time that’s best for every customer. Seventh Sense eases your stress of having to figure out the perfect send-time and day for your email campaigns. The AI-based platform figures out the best timing and email frequency for each contact based on when they’re opening emails. The tool is primarily geared toward HubSpot and Marketo customers.

    Sources indicate that phrasee uses artificial intelligence to help you write more effective subject lines. With its AI-based Natural Language Generation system, Phrasee uses data-driven insights to generate millions of natural-sounding copy variants that match your brand voice. The model is end-to-end, meaning when you feed the results back to Phrasee, the prediction model rebuilds so it can continuously learn from your audience.

    Sources indicate that hubSpot Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is an integral tool for the Human Content team. It uses machine learning to determine how search engines understand and categorize your content. HubSpot SEO helps you improve your search engine rankings and outrank your competitors. Search engines reward websites that organize their content around core subjects, or topic clusters. HubSpot SEO helps you discover and rank for the topics that matter to your business and customers.

    Recent findings suggest that when you’re limited to testing two variables against each other at a time, it can take months to get the results you’re looking for. Evolv AI lets you test all your ideas at once. It uses advanced algorithms to identify the top-performing concepts, combine them with each other, and repeat the process to achieve the best site experience.

    Industry observers note that acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include big brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and manufacturer-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

    According to recent reports, marketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool shows you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for new content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

    In a recent development, copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

    In a recent development, yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert latest shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

    Sources indicate that albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

    Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

    It has been revealed that there are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, new marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. But for now, this list should give you a good starting point on your way to implementing AI into your marketing mix.

Frontier LLMs paired with AST analyzers, decompilers (Ghidra, WABT, ILSpy), and SMT solvers like Z3 reconstruct clean-room source code from minified bundles in minutes.

    Recent findings suggest that over the past few months at Soltrix Studios, we built Syferit, an open-core, 100% offline build-time code defense engine. We just shipped Syferit v2.1.1, and rather than just writing marketing claims about it, we put it through two real tests: a massive production Next.js app and a public 60 FPS JS + WebAssembly crackme.

    Here is what changed in v2.1, what actually broke along the way, and where you can try breaking it yourself.

    When we ran early v2.0 builds on a real production Next.js codebase (209 chunks including heavy dependencies like three.js and @ffmpeg/ffmpeg), we hit a wall:.

    That benchmark forced three real engineering fixes in Syferit v2.1.1:.

    The result on that exact same 209-chunk Next.js app:.

    According to recent reports, syferit runs strictly at build time (zero runtime dependencies, zero network calls, zero telemetry). Out of the box, its default v2-quantum-rns preset hardens production builds across four layers:.

    Recent findings suggest that client-side code still has to run inside V8 on the user's machine. Nothing on earth makes browser JavaScript "100% unbreakable." A determined reverse engineer with Chrome DevTools, Frida, or enough time can still set breakpoints on DOM mutations or inspect fetch() payloads at the network boundary.

    The real goal of Syferit is raising the cost of static analysis, automated AI cloning agents, and casual decompilation from "5 minutes with an LLM" to "serious manual reverse engineering," while keeping build times fast and runtime overhead near zero.

    Instead of asking anyone to take our word on runtime overhead, we built a live 60 FPS browser game and crackme called SYFER-DRIFT: The Enclave Heist:.

    Every single frame at 60 FPS, the game runs a cross-runtime JavaScript + WebAssembly verification pass protected by stock Syferit v2.1.1. There is also a "Run 1,000x Enclave Burst" button right in the telemetry bar so you can measure live latency in your own browser while driving. On Chrome, 1,000 consecutive JS Micro-VM + WASM MBA calls finish in roughly 8 to 45 milliseconds (~0.008 to 0.046 ms per call) with zero dropped frames.

    If you are into reverse engineering, you can also download the 100% offline bundle (vault-engine.js, enclave.wasm, and challenge-cli.js) straight from the challenge page (or on Crackmes.one once approved). Every lock is deterministically solvable with zero brute-forcing, and solving all three keys decrypts a hidden flag and a note from our team.

    #206801. Latest Update: Do art fairs care about non-VIP visitors?

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1406 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Theartnewspaper ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Do art fairs care about non-VIP visitors?

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1406 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theartnewspaper

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, october’s Paris art week had become the must-attend fixture of the international art market calendar, particularly for wealthy Americans.
    • Industry observers note that “It’s vital to be in Paris,” said Chris Sharp, the Los Angeles gallerist and founder of Post-Fair, a boutique California-based event that held its first edition in the French capital this October.
    • The previous weekend, Paris had been rocked by mass demonstrations that in some areas had escalated into riots and looting.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, october’s Paris art week had become the must-attend fixture of the international art market calendar, particularly for wealthy Americans. No other city could match the range and quality of the French capital’s art fairs and exhibitions, both at public museums and private foundations. And what about all those charming restaurants, cafes and shops?

    Industry observers note that “It’s vital to be in Paris,” said Chris Sharp, the Los Angeles gallerist and founder of Post-Fair, a boutique California-based event that held its first edition in the French capital this October. “Paris is the undisputed capital of the art world—once a year,” Sharp added, speaking at Post-Fair’s preview on 19 October, in the chic Marais district. Nearby, someone had sprayed “mort aux riches” across the window of a bank.

    The previous weekend, Paris had been rocked by mass demonstrations that in some areas had escalated into riots and looting. Further demonstrations, highlighting the neglected state of France’s secondary schools, the ever-rising cost of living and other grievances, had been planned in Paris and other French cities on the afternoon of Saturday 24 October. Unemployment in France for those aged 15 to 24 at the moment stands at 21.5%, almost three times the rate in neighbouring Germany.

    On Tuesday 20 October, the day of the ultra-exclusive Avant-Première pre-preview of Art Basel Paris in the Grand Palais, the French activist collective Pillage de Classe (class plunder) posted a message on Instagram exhorting protesters to “take back” the famous Belle Époque exhibition hall on Saturday, the penultimate day of the week’s flagship fair.

    Art Basel Paris has been held in the historic Grand Palais since 2024.

    Of course, the Grand Palais was not stormed, Bastille-style. In the highly unlikely event of protesters managing to “take back” the building, they would have been disappointed, just as revolutionaries had been in 1789, when they discovered the prison they had liberated contained just seven detainees. Art Basel Paris, taking no risks, had closed the event two days early on Friday evening (after an excoriating letter from France's gallery association to fair director Karim Crippa, Art Basel recompensed exhibitors 20% of their stand fees).

    The mega-gallery Hauser & Wirth took even fewer risks, emptying its stand the day before, leaving three paintings by the local artist Hélène Delprat. The fair had been shortened to three VIP preview days plus just one day for the general public. Satellite fairs, like Paris Internationale and Post-Fair, closed at lunchtime on Saturday.

    Sources indicate that that Saturday afternoon, more than 100,000 people duly turned out to demonstrate. However, these proved predominantly peaceful and were confined by the police to the outskirts of the city.

    Sources indicate that the disruption in Paris had surely been a momentary blip. And Art Basel’s ultra-wealthy invitees, which the top end of the international art trade likes to call the “right kind of people”, had already been and gone. But what about the reputational impact?

    “The collateral damage is substantial considering the whole point of being in Paris is to let yourself surrender to its myriad charms,” mentioned Andrew Terner, a New York-based private dealer and collector, speaking in the immediate aftermath of the early closure.

    The French authorities blamed “ultra-left radical groups” for the violence that had marred weeks of otherwise peaceful protests, begun in September by discontented teenage lycée students. Pillage de Classe is certainly a left-wing radical group; it views Art Basel Paris as a luxury playground in which art is used by the ultra-wealthy to protect their capital from taxation.

    But maybe (leaving aside its desire to take the Grand Palais by storm) Pillage de Classe has a point, at least with regard to the fair’s top French clients. In France, the net worth of the country’s 500 wealthiest individuals has ballooned from 6% of the country’s GDP in 1996 to 42% in 2024, according to a much-cited article in the French business magazine Challenges. Tax reforms introduced by President Macron in 2017 excluded stocks, financial assets (including art) and corporate investments from wealth tax calculations.

    Moreover, in 2003 the French government had granted tax breaks of up to 75% for private individuals and 60% for corporations that supported the arts. This encouraged investment in glitzy private foundations, such as the Fondation Louis Vuitton, François Pinault’s Bourse de Commerce, the Fondation Cartier and the newly opened Île Seguin luxury hotel and Large art centre, which have become such an alluring feature of the Paris art scene for international visitors. According to research by Apollo magazine, Bernard Arnault’s LVMH luxury group received an aggregate tax break of €518.1m between 2007 and 2017 to set against the €790m the corporation spent building the Frank Gehry-designed Fondation Louis Vuitton.

    The ultra-wealthy have also grown a lot wealthier in the US in recent years. The share of the nation’s wealth held by the richest 0.0001% (around 200 individuals) is now more than seven times what it was in 1980, according to a November Substack posted by the Nobel Prize-winning economist Paul Krugman.

    Sources indicate that today’s art market is dominated by the world’s wealthiest people buying the world’s most expensive art. Most of these people are pretty old. This is not a good look now that the Democrats have won a landslide victory in the US midterm elections, driven by a massive turnout of young voters. Authoritarian rulers like Viktor Orbán in Hungary and Aleksandar Vučić in Serbia have been voted out of office. Young people have been protesting en masse about their diminished life chances in France and more than a dozen other countries across the world.

    Industry observers note that suddenly, ordinary people matter again. The young matter. But do they matter at art fairs?

    It has been revealed that take ticket-pricing. In October, the general public were charged £48 each to attend Frieze London, with students being asked to pay £32. Does Frieze, which is owned by the billionaire Ari Emanuel, the former chief executive of the US entertainment conglomerate Endeavor, want to actively discourage young people from visiting? Or is that ticket price an acknowledgement that pretty much the only students who can now afford to attend the UK’s art colleges come from more affluent backgrounds?

    Recent findings suggest that the following week, Art Basel Paris, part of James Murdoch’s Lupa Systems investment portfolio, was charging €47 for a standard day pass and €30 for a student ticket. “The galleries pay for the fair. Visitors are a side business,” says Magnus Resch, a New York-based author and art market entrepreneur. According to Resch’s back-of-an-envelope calculations, stand fees generate at least €15m, while tickets bring in less than €3m. “Charging the public €47 isn’t about the money. It’s about keeping the fair exclusive.” (Art Basel does not reveal detailed breakdowns of its revenue streams.).

    “It is crucial for the public to visit an art fair,” states Guillaume Sultana, whose contemporary art gallery exhibited on the upper level of Art Basel Paris, where footfall is slower than down on the ground floor among the mega-galleries. “But a lot of general visitors on the weekend are a bit frustrated because public tickets are very expensive.”.

    Sultana acknowledges that “the main business is done during the very first days of an art fair, always”. Despite the fair being truncated, Sultana describes the experience as “very good”, having sold a painting by the young Syrian artist Osama Al Rayyan during the preview for €15,000, among other works.

    In the funfair-mirror optics of the international art market, €15,000 might appear a relatively “affordable” price point. But traditionally, sensible collectors have been advised to spend no more than 5% of their available wealth on art. So, whoever bought that Al Rayan painting, should, theoretically, have had €300,000 of spare cash available. For would-be younger collectors in today’s tough economic conditions, these are intimidating figures, unless they can call on the bank of mum and dad.

    In a recent development, collecting art is in serious danger of being perceived as something that old, rich people do. With so many established collectors ageing and selling, rather than buying, and a democratic wave pushing back against oligarchical wealth, this might be a good moment for the art market to think more about inclusivity than exclusivity, to take a broader view of who might be the “right kind” of people.

    After all, who wants “death to the rich” sprayed across their gallery window?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    โดย Nokka (นก-กา) | 26 พฤศจิกายน 2569.

    บทความนี้เขียนโดย AI (โมเดล glm-5.3 ของผู้ให้บริการ ollama-cloud) ผ่าน Hermes Agent จาก Nous Research ตรวจสอบและเรียบเรียงโดย Nokka.

    In a recent development, วันที่ 24 พฤศจิกายน (ค.ศ. 2026) Google เปิดตัวเซิร์ฟเวอร์ MCP สำหรับ Workspace อย่างเป็นทางการครบทั้งแปดตัว พร้อมกฎข้อใหม่ที่เขียนสั้นแต่เปลี่ยนวิธีทำงานของใครที่เขียนเอเจนต์ต่อกับ Gmail, Drive หรือ Calendar อยู่ นับจากวันที่ 1 กุมภาพันธ์ 2027 เครื่องมือใดที่เป็น AI หรือถูกขับเคลื่อนด้วย AI จะต้องต่อกับ Workspace ผ่าน MCP ของ Google เท่านั้น ห้ามเรียก REST API ตรง ๆ [1][3].

    ปัญหาอยู่ตรงที่เมื่อเปิดเซิร์ฟเวอร์ Gmail ดูจริง ๆ จะพบว่ามันค้นเมลได้ อ่านเมลได้ สร้างฉบับร่างได้ แต่ส่งเมลไม่ได้ [4].

    ข้อความบังคับอยู่ในเอกสารเพิ่มเติมชื่อ Workspace AI Tools Addendum ที่แนบกับข้อตกลงใช้บริการ ผมอ่านจากตัวเอกสารจริง ข้อแรกระบุตรง ๆ ว่าเครื่องมือเข้าถึง Workspace ต้องใช้ MCP ของ Google ในกรณีที่เครื่องมือนั้นเป็น AI Agent, เป็น AI Harness หรือถูกขับเคลื่อนด้วยโมเดล AI หรือบริการที่ใช้โมเดล AI [2].

    ข้อถัดไปห้ามพรางตัวเอเจนต์ให้พ้นการจำแนก เมื่อทำผิด Google สามารถตัดสิทธิ์การเข้าถึงหรือระงับบัญชีได้ [2].

    ข้อบังคับเรื่อง MCP ครอบเฉพาะเครื่องมือ AI ในบันทึกประจำรุ่นเดือนตุลาคม Google เขียนเองว่าแอปที่ไม่ใช่เอเจนต์ AI เช่นโปรแกรมที่เรียก REST API เท่านั้น ไม่ได้รับผลกระทบจากการเปลี่ยนแปลงเรื่องการจำแนก OAuth client ครั้งนี้ [3].

    ส่วนการจัดชั้นโควตาใหม่เป็นอีกเรื่องหนึ่ง ใช้กับ API ของ Workspace โดยรวม ไม่ใช่เฉพาะเอเจนต์ [1].

    คู่มือทางการของเซิร์ฟเวอร์ Gmailระบุว่ามีเครื่องมือให้ใช้สิบตัว แบ่งเป็นสามกลุ่มงาน [4].

    ทว่าคู่มือไม่ใช่ขอบเขตทั้งหมด หน้าโควตาทางการของ Google ซึ่งอัปเดตล่าสุด 24 พฤศจิกายน 2026 วันเดียวกับที่เปิดใช้งาน ขึ้นทะเบียนเครื่องมือของ Gmail ไว้ 31 ตัว โดยแปดตัวมีดอกจันกำกับว่าต้องมีสิทธิ์พันธมิตร [7] เหลือเครื่องมือสาธารณะ 23 ตัว รวมถึงการย้ายข้อความลงถังขยะและสแปมที่คู่มือไม่ได้ระบุว่ามีให้ใช้ ตัวเลข 23 ตรงกับผลยิง tools/list ในรายงานของ [6] และชุดงานที่ [5] ระบุว่าเปิดให้สาธารณะก็ตรงกัน.

    การส่งเมล ตอบกลับ ส่งต่อ และการแก้ไขฉบับร่างที่สร้างไว้แล้ว ไม่ปรากฏในเครื่องมือสาธารณะทั้งชุด เครื่องมือเหล่านี้มีอยู่จริงบนเซิร์ฟเวอร์เดียวกัน แต่ถูกกักไว้ให้เฉพาะพันธมิตรที่ได้รับอนุมัติ สองรายงานสื่อที่ตรวจแยกกันยืนยันตรงกันว่าหน้าโควตาของ Google ระบุว่าเครื่องมือกลุ่มนี้ต้องมีสิทธิ์พันธมิตรและยังไม่เปิดทั่วไป [5][6].

    ผลที่ตามมาคือลำดับงานที่พังกลางทาง ลองนึกภาพสถานการณ์นี้ คุณพิมพ์สั่งตัวช่วยว่า ร่างอีเมลตอบลูกค้าเรื่องงบประมาณ เอเจนต์ค้นเมลเจอ ร่างให้เรียบร้อย คุณอ่านแล้วคอมเมนต์ว่าเพิ่มส่วนลดและเปลี่ยนโทนให้ทางการขึ้น.

    จังหวะนี้พังทันที เพราะการแก้ฉบับร่างเดิมไม่ใช่เครื่องมือสาธารณะ เอเจนต์มีทางเดียวคือสร้างร่างใหม่อีกฉบับแล้วทิ้งอันเก่าไว้ให้คุณลบเอง.

    ฝั่ง Drive ก็เจอแบบเดียวกันในระดับเบากว่า เอเจนต์สร้างรายงานเสร็จแต่ย้ายเข้าโฟลเดอร์ที่ถูกต้องหรือแชร์ให้ทีมเองไม่ได้ [5].

    รายละเอียดเชิงเทคนิคสำหรับคนจะลอง: เซิร์ฟเวอร์แต่ละตัวอยู่ที่โดเมนของตัวเอง เช่น gmailmcp.googleapis.com โดยมีปลายทางหลัก /mcp/v1 และปลายทาง /mcp/v1self สำหรับโปรแกรมที่ไม่รองรับการยืนยันผ่านแบบฟอร์ม สิทธิ์ที่ขอคือชุดเดียวกับ REST เช่น gmail.readonly กับ gmail.compose [4].

    อีกข้อในเอกสารเพิ่มเติมที่คนเขียนเอเจนต์จะรู้สึกถึงที่สุดคือการห้ามเก็บข้อมูลจำพวก Google Technical Information เกิน 30 วัน คำนิยามของข้อมูลกลุ่มนี้ครอบคลุมถึง vector embeddings, ดัชนีความจำ โปรไฟล์ผู้ใช้ และผังความสัมพันธ์ในองค์กรที่สร้างจากข้อมูล Workspace โดยที่ตัวข้อมูลของผู้ใช้เช่นเนื้อความอีเมลไม่ได้ถูกลบตามกฎ 30 วันนี้ ส่วนที่ห้ามเก็บคือผลสังเคราะห์ที่เอเจนต์สร้างขึ้นจากการใช้งาน [2].

    แปลง่าย ๆ ว่าตัวช่วยที่สร้างความจำระยะยาวจากกล่องจดหมายเพื่อตอบคำถามเรื่องสัญญาปีที่แล้ว จะต้องสร้างดัชนีใหม่ทุกเดือนหรือปล่อยความสามารถนี้ไป.

    พร้อมกันนั้นยังห้ามใช้ข้อมูลไปเทรนโมเดลหรือสร้างผลิตภัณฑ์ที่แข่งกับ Workspace และเมื่อผู้ใช้ถอดเอเจนต์ออก ข้อมูลที่เก็บไว้ต้องถูกลบทิ้งด้วย [2].

    ระดับพื้นฐานฟรี ได้ 5,000 คำขอต่อวันต่อโปรเจกต์ต่อผลิตภัณฑ์ แต่คำขอหนึ่งครั้งไม่เท่ากันเสมอไป เครื่องมือที่ต้องเรียก API หลายชั้นเบื้องหลังจะถูกนับเป็นหลายคำขอ [3].

    โควตานี้แชร์กันทั้งโปรเจกต์ ผลิตภัณฑ์เล็กที่มีผู้ใช้หลายคนจะชนเพดานเร็วกว่าที่คิด ตัวอย่างจากรายงานของสื่อเทคโนโลยีคือเครื่องมือค้นเมลหนึ่งครั้งถูกนับเป็นสิบคำขอ เอเจนต์ที่ทำแต่การค้นเมลจะได้ราวห้าร้อยครั้งต่อวันรวมทุกผู้ใช้ [5].

    ระดับ Scaled สำหรับงานหนักเริ่มคิดเงินวันที่ 1 เมษายน 2027 โดยหน้าทางการสองหน้าระบุต่างกันเอง หนึ่งบอกคิดตั้งแต่คำขอแรกของ MCP อีกหน้าบอกคิดเฉพาะส่วนที่เกินโควตาฟรีต่อวัน ส่วนโควตาฟรีขนาดใหญ่ของ REST ยังอยู่กับการเรียกแบบเดิม ซึ่งอ่านได้ว่าเป็นโครงสร้างราคาที่ผลักให้เอเจนต์ต้องอยู่บนเส้นทางของ Google [1][3][5].

    ความเห็นส่วนตัว: ผมอ่านแล้วเห็นสองด้านชัดทั้งคู่ ด้านความปลอดภัย เหตุผลของ Google มีน้ำหนักจริง เพราะโทเคนที่ได้รับมาไม่ได้แปลว่าเจตนาของคน อีเมลฉบับหนึ่งที่เขียนว่าให้ส่งอีเมลสิบฉบับข้างหน้าไปที่อยู่นี้ คือความเสี่ยงโจมตีแบบพรอมต์อินเจกชันที่มีอยู่จริง การบังคับให้ทุกเอเจนต์เดินผ่านประตูบานเดียวที่ผู้ดูแลองค์กรตั้งกฎยืนยันจากมนุษย์และบันทึกการใช้งานไว้ได้ ทำให้ผู้ดูแลคุมได้จริง แต่อีกด้านคือของที่ปิดไว้ให้เฉพาะพันธมิตร คนทำผลิตภัณฑ์อิสระจะได้เล่นในสนามที่ตัดสิทธิ์เฉพาะกิจ และเส้นทางเดิมที่เคยเปิดกว้างก็ถูกปิดลงพร้อมกัน สำหรับทีมไทยที่ทำตัวช่วยอีเมลหรือระบบออโตเมชัน AI ต่อ Workspace ผมว่าอย่ารอถึงมกราคม ประเมินว่าผลิตภัณฑ์ตัวเองอยู่ด้านไหนของกฎเสียตั้งแต่ตอนนี้ครับ.

    ถ้าคุณกำลังย้ายเอเจนต์ไป MCP อยู่และเจอปัญหาอะไร คอมเมนต์เล่าไว้ได้ครับ และถ้าบทนี้ช่วยได้ แชร์ให้ทีมที่ทำงานกับ Workspace ด้วยก็จะดีมาก.

    fm-cli is in the official Omarchy package repo

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (203 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • fm-cli, my little terminal client for Fastmail, is now an optional package in the official Omarchy repo.
    • On Omarchy, open the menu with Super + Space, choose Install > Package, and type fm-cli.
    • Then sign in with fm-cli auth login, which opens Fastmail's consent page in your browser.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I have been waiting on this one. fm-cli, my little terminal client for Fastmail, is now an optional package in the official Omarchy repo. It is not on the default install, which is fine: it is there if you want it, and it is not in anyone's way if you don't.

    On Omarchy, open the menu with Super + Space, choose Install > Package, and type fm-cli. Or, from a terminal:.

    Then sign in with fm-cli auth login, which opens Fastmail's consent page in your browser. That is it.

    In a recent development, fm-cli is a small Go client for Fastmail's JMAP API. It gives you a full-screen mail app in the terminal, commands that print JSON, a live watch over Fastmail's push connection, and offline reading and drafting. It is also the engine behind the Fastmail plugin for Omarchy.

    The package that landed today is 0.3.3. Newer releases, up to 0.3.6, are on GitHub and still installable with mise if you want the latest. I'll work on getting the official package caught up.

    If you are not on Omarchy, the usual options are still there: mise, autonomix-cli, and the .deb, .rpm and tarball releases.

    Originally posted on blog.ninepointlabs.com.

    #206792. PDF to Text in Your Browser: pdf-lib Can't Extract Text, but pdf.js Can

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1231 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dev ↗ Open Full Page

    PDF to Text in Your Browser: pdf-lib Can't Extract Text, but pdf.js Can

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1231 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If you want the words out of a PDF without uploading the file anywhere, the answer is one function: page.getTextContent() from Mozilla's pdf.js.
    • Below: what pdf.js does, the exact code already running in one of my production tools, and a real test on two real PDFs.
    • My PDF merger runs on pdf-lib, so when I needed text out of a PDF, I reached for the same library first.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you want the words out of a PDF without uploading the file anywhere, the answer is one function: page.getTextContent() from Mozilla's pdf.js. And if you already build PDF tools with pdf-lib — the library from my merging post — here is the thing nobody tells you until you waste an afternoon on it: pdf-lib cannot extract text at all. Both "do PDFs in JavaScript", but they do opposite halves of the job, and picking the wrong one is the most common dead end in browser PDF work.

    Below: what pdf.js does, the exact code already running in one of my production tools, and a real test on two real PDFs.

    My PDF merger runs on pdf-lib, so when I needed text out of a PDF, I reached for the same library first. I checked the only way that settles it:.

    pdf-lib 1.17.1 exposes 46 methods on PDFDocument.prototype, and not one of them mentions text or extraction. It can load a document, copy pages between documents, draw new text onto a page, and save the result. Reading the text already in a page is simply not in its vocabulary. That is a design boundary, not a missing feature: pdf-lib is a document builder, and extraction belongs to a document reader.

    Industry observers note that A PDF does not store text the way a .txt file does. It stores positioned fragments — a string here, a string there, each with coordinates — and the order those fragments sit in the file is not necessarily the order a person reads them. pdf.js, Mozilla's open-source PDF parser, parses that structure and hands you the fragments per page:.

    Industry observers note that getTextContent() returns one entry per text fragment, each with a str property. Join them and you have the page's words — the entire extraction step. Everything else in a real tool is interface: file picker, progress label, copy button, download-as-.txt button.

    According to recent reports, two things worth knowing before you trust the output blindly. First, the join matters: the example joins fragments with a space, which is what my link extractor does. Nutrient's guide improves on this by checking each item's hasEOL flag and inserting a newline where the PDF ends a line — better for prose, where a space-join can glue a heading to the next paragraph. Second, pdf.js reads the text layer. A scanned PDF is pictures, not text, and getTextContent() will honestly return nothing for those pages. That is the boundary between extraction and OCR — a different tool (Tesseract.js) for a different problem.

    This is live code from ToolNest's PDF link extractor, running pdf.js in visitors' browsers — same library, same version, same pattern:.

    Recent findings suggest that two details in there earned their place the hard way. The library loads from jsDelivr first and falls back to unpkg if the first CDN fails. And the worker script is pinned to the same version as the main script, because a version mismatch fails silently — the document just never loads.

    The extraction loop is the heart of the tool, and it is also where the link extractor gets its text to scan:.

    Notice what it does not do: the file bytes come from file.arrayBuffer() — the file the visitor picked, read locally. No upload, no endpoint, no server anywhere in the path. The browser parses the PDF in a Web Worker, and closing the tab leaves nothing behind — a contract never has to trust anyone's retention policy.

    Recent findings suggest that I ran the same library version (pdfjs-dist 3.11.174) against two real files from my own site — Pagelyra's free sample PDFs. Test script: /tmp/pdftext-test/extract-test.js, Node v24.22.1, 2026-11-26, after npm install pdfjs-dist@3.11.174 pdf-lib:.

    The journal sample is mostly form labels, returned exactly, blank lines included as __________ underscores. The chapter sample is prose, back in reading order, dialogue quotes intact: "Who is it for, Gran? The key." "Whoever the garden chooses.".

    Two honest notes. The 184 ms includes the library warming up — the second file took 15 ms, the honest per-file cost once loaded. Node also printed warnings about missing standard font data; they did not affect the output, and they are a Node-only artifact. The point is not the milliseconds: a four-page PDF gives up its text in well under a second, with no server, on a library version already proven in production.

    Scanned PDFs return nothing. If the page is a photograph of a page, there is no text layer, and getTextContent() returns an empty list. Say so in your UI — "no text found, this looks like a scanned document" — instead of showing a blank box and letting the user assume the tool is broken.

    It has been revealed that reading order is not guaranteed. pdf.js returns fragments in the order they sit in the file, which for multi-column layouts can mean the left column's second paragraph arrives after the right column's first. Single-column documents read correctly, as the two test files show. For two-column papers, expect interleaving — sort fragments by coordinates before joining.

    It has been revealed that the worker setup has two silent failure modes. If you forget to set workerSrc, pdf.js falls back to a "fake worker" on the main thread — extraction still works, but a 50-page PDF freezes the page while it parses. And if the worker version does not match the main library version, loading hangs with no error at all. Both are documented in the w3tweaks guide on PDF.js extraction — pin both scripts to one version string, as the production code does.

    According to recent reports, can pdf-lib extract text from a PDF? No. I verified it directly: pdf-lib 1.17.1's PDFDocument has 46 prototype methods and none of them reads text. pdf-lib builds and modifies PDFs; extraction is pdf.js's job.

    In a recent development, does this work on scanned PDFs? No — a scan has no text layer to read, so getTextContent() returns nothing for those pages. Scanned documents need OCR (Tesseract.js runs in the browser). Check whether you can select text in your PDF reader first: if you can select it, pdf.js can extract it.

    How large a PDF can the browser handle? No hard limit, but the whole file sits in memory, and a 5 MB PDF can expand well beyond its file size once parsed. Ordinary documents run in milliseconds, as the test above indicates.

    Industry observers note that is my file uploaded anywhere? No. The file is read with file.arrayBuffer(), parsed by pdf.js in a Web Worker, and the text is produced in your tab. There is no server endpoint involved at all — the entire reason to build it this way.

    Sources indicate that PDF to text in the browser is a solved problem, but only if you pick the reading library: pdf.js, getDocument() then getTextContent() per page, worker pinned to the same version. pdf-lib is the wrong tool for this half of the job — and knowing that saves you the afternoon I spent learning it.

    Recent findings suggest that toolNest's PDF link extractor already runs this exact code in production — it reads the same text layer to find URLs — and the PDF merger from my earlier post covers the other half with pdf-lib. Between the two libraries, the browser does the whole job, and your file never leaves your machine.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • In a recent development, women who changed their usual lunchtime drink lost 41 per cent more weight over 18 months.
    • Swapping diet drinks for water could help people lose more weight.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that women who changed their usual lunchtime drink lost 41 per cent more weight over 18 months. What made the difference?

    In a recent development, women who changed their usual lunchtime drink lost 41 per cent more weight over 18 months. What made the difference?

    Swapping diet drinks for water could help people lose more weight.

    Women with type 2 diabetes who make the switch lose around 41 percent more weight over 18 months than those who continue drinking diet beverages.

    They are also twice as likely to achieve diabetes remission during a structured weight-management programme.

    The findings raise a question about whether a drink’s calorie count tells the whole story about its effects on weight.

    Sweet taste without the accompanying energy might influence appetite signals.

    The results suggest that everyday drink choices could play a useful supporting role in longer-term weight management.

    The research involved around 80 women who were overweight or had obesity, had type 2 diabetes and regularly consumed diet drinks.

    Researchers randomly assigned them either to replace their usual diet beverage with water after lunch five times a week or to continue drinking it.

    Both groups took part in a six-month weight-loss programme followed by a year devoted to maintaining their progress.

    By the end, women assigned to water had lost an average of 6.82 kg, compared with 4.85 kg among those continuing with diet drinks.

    The difference amounted to almost 2 kg of additional weight loss across the programme.

    The water group also showed greater improvements in measures including fasting blood glucose, insulin resistance and blood fats.

    Diabetes remission was reported in 90 percent of women assigned to water, compared with 45 percent of those continuing diet beverages.

    It has been revealed that dr Hamid R. Farshchi, study co-author, stated:.

    “It’s a small change with the potential for a big impact on long-term health outcomes.”.

    The brain may respond differently when a sweet taste arrives without the energy normally supplied by sugar.

    In a separate experiment involving around 75 adults, participants reported greater hunger after consuming sucralose than sugar, and the sweetener altered activity in the hypothalamus, a brain region involved in appetite regulation (Chakravartti et al., 2025).

    However, hunger ratings after sucralose did not differ from those after water, so the findings do not establish that sweetened drinks necessarily make people hungrier than plain water.

    The mismatch between sweetness and energy might help explain some appetite responses, but whether it contributed to the weight-loss difference remains unknown.

    The study was published in the journal Diabetes (Farshchi Nasr et al., 2025).
